cacrepAreas.name: Professional Counseling Orientation and Ethical Practice

domains.name: Professional Practice and Ethics
domains.description: Counselors' knowledge, skills, and abilities related to maintaining proper administrative and clinical protocols.

tasks.A: Assess your (the counselor) competency to work with a specific client
tasks.B: Understand statistical concepts and methods in research
tasks.H: Review payment, fees, and insurance benefits
tasks.I: Explain counseling processes, procedures, risks, and benefits
tasks.J: Explain uses and limits of social media
tasks.K: Inform clients about the legal aspects of counseling
tasks.M: Discuss confidentiality as it applies to electronic communication
tasks.N: Establish group rules, expectations, and termination criteria
tasks.O: Assess competency to provide informed consent
tasks.P: Monitor the therapeutic relationship and build trust as needed
tasks.R: Provide adequate accommodations for clients with disabilities
tasks.T: Provide referral sources if counseling services are inadequate/inappropriate
tasks.U: Advocate for professional and client issues
tasks.W: Create and maintain documentation appropriate for each aspect of the counseling process

domains.name: Intake, Assessment, and Diagnosis
domains.description: Counselors' knowledge, skills, and abilities to effectively conduct client intake, assessment, and diagnosis.

tasks.I: Determine the appropriate modality of treatment
tasks.J: Assess the presenting problem and level of distress
tasks.K: Evaluate an individual's level of mental health functioning
tasks.M: Select, use, and interpret appropriate assessment instruments
tasks.S: Conduct ongoing assessment for at-risk behaviors (i.e., suicide, homicide, self/other injury, and relationship violence)
tasks.T: Use pre-test and post-test measures to assess outcomes

domains.name: Areas of Clinical Focus
domains.description: Counselors' knowledge and skills related to areas of clients' concern(s).

tasks.A: Adjustment related to physical loss/injury/medical condition

domains.name: Treatment Planning
domains.description: Counselors' knowledge, skills, and abilities to develop an effective course of treatment.

tasks.A: Collaborate with client to establish treatment goals and objectives
tasks.B: Establish short- and long-term counseling goals consistent with clients' diagnoses
tasks.C: Identify barriers affecting client goal attainment
tasks.D: Identify strengths that improve the likelihood of goal attainment
tasks.E: Refer to different levels of treatment (e.g., outpatient, inpatient, residential, etc.)
tasks.F: Refer to others for concurrent treatment
tasks.K: Use assessment instrument results to facilitate client decision making
tasks.L: Review and revise the treatment plan
tasks.M: Engage clients in review of progress toward treatment goals
tasks.N: Collaborate with other providers and client support systems (documentation and report writing)
tasks.O: Discuss with clients the integration and maintenance of therapeutic progress
tasks.P: Educate client to the value of treatment plan compliance

domains.name: Counseling Skills and Interventions
domains.description: Counselors' knowledge, skills, and abilities to conduct effective counseling.

tasks.A: Align intervention with client's developmental level
tasks.B: Align intervention with counseling modality (individual, couple, family, or group)
tasks.C: Align intervention with client population (e.g., veterans, minorities, disenfranchised, disabled)
tasks.D: Implement individual counseling in relation to a plan of treatment
tasks.I: Address family composition and cultural considerations
tasks.J: Evaluate and explain systemic patterns of interaction
tasks.M: Guide clients in the development of skills or strategies for dealing with their problems
tasks.O: Help facilitate clients' motivation to make the changes they desire
tasks.R: Educate client about transference and defense mechanisms
tasks.X: Provide distance counseling or telemental health
tasks.Y: Provide education resources (e.g., stress management, assertiveness training, divorce adjustment)
tasks.AH: Use linking and blocking in a group context
tasks.AJ: Model giving and receiving of feedback
tasks.AM: Explore the influence of family of origin patterns and themes
tasks.AN: Address the impact of social support network
tasks.AP: Promote and encourage interactions among group members
tasks.AQ: Promote and encourage interactions with the group leader
tasks.AR: Use psychoeducation as a part of the group process
tasks.AS: Explain phases in the group process
tasks.AT: Identify and discuss group themes and patterns
tasks.AU: Create intervention based on the stage of group development
tasks.AW: Address the potential interaction of members outside of the group

domains.name: Core Counseling Attributes
domains.description: Behaviors, traits, and dispositions of effective counselors.

tasks.A: Awareness of self and impact on clients
tasks.D: Demonstrate knowledge of and sensitivity to gender orientation and gender issues
tasks.E: Demonstrate knowledge of and sensitivity to multicultural issues
tasks.I: Foster the emergence of group therapeutic factors
tasks.M: Use foundational listening, attending, and reflecting skills
